meeting.title: Madison Valley Hospital + Mulesoft: Automation/Integration Technical Discovery

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Mark hi Briana, how's it going? Very good, how are you sir doing?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: All right, guys.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Nice to meet you both. There's going to be a lot of faces on here.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah, we're missing the main ones.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Yeah, we are. Introduce yourself. In the meantime, I take it you guys are on the prior Ra side?

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yes. It's actually not my main job. I'm actually a supervisor for the front end of the hospital, but I do prior... [Laughter] Okay, because right now I don't have anyone else to do them. So here we are.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Here we are. Nice to meet you, Kailash. Good to see you.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Good to see you guys again.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: Yes, you too, sir. Hello, wow, thank God for Google Meet, Zoom, can you imagine trying to do this in person, all these people? Kate, are we waiting on anyone else?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I don't think so. Three? Am I forgetting anybody? Yeah, I think we did. We did have one of our infusion nurses who was going to try and stop it, but I think she just had a patient walk up that she needs to get started, so she may hop on later.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: Yeah.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: I was going to be the only additional one.

content.speaker: Speaker 3
content.text: I was just going to update her on everything.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Okay, there we go.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text:
This is recording, guys, so I can always send you the recording after if you want to rewatch it. All right, I'm going to kick us off real quick. We small-talked with introductions, but we will formally go around and briefly introduce ourselves. Again, if I can get this all right, let me just... So we're on the same page.
It's like how this called... I'm thinking we'll go and feel free to correct me or make adjustments or recommendations. Of course, we have a lot of people to go through, so I'll try not to be too redundant, but we'll do brief introductions on everybody on the screen. We've got a couple of new faces. We'll briefly recap what we discussed last call and then talk about the prior authorization use case that we talked about.
If there are any other workflows that you guys would like to explore automating, then we'd be happy to talk about them, but we really want to be clear on what we're solving for, at least as far as Phase I goes. A lot of times people will get access to the platform and think of use cases down the road. More than happy to phase this out in separate approaches if you think prior authorization might be more appropriate for Phase II to do together in Phase I.
Totally up to you. After we recap, we'll go into the technical scoping of that project. That's why I brought Kailash and Ryan. There are our Salesforce recommendations, recommended implementation partners that would help you guys implement the solution.
Given that we're all aligned, the really the main goal is to be crystal clear on next steps if we are agreed that Mulesoft is a solution here. What that looks like even past the decision aligning on go-live dates and everything that needs to happen before then. Anything that you guys would like to cover specifically, I didn't just mention.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Did you mention cost?

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text:
That's the point of this call. I can give you a ballpark at the end, but the reason I brought in the implementation partners is to scope out the work. It varies depending on how many documents, what we're integrating, what systems, and how many.
So there'll be software costs and implementation costs, but more than happy to share a ballpark to bet that out.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text: Perfect.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: I guess we can get that way. Do you have a number in mind that you guys had set aside to solve for this?

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
Well, I think that's going to be department-specific. So for each of the different pieces that we're looking to add into this, they're going to have their own values and potential RI goals.
So I can speak for the pharmacy in general. If we were to find a service and I may have gone over this briefly with you before, but we're able to find a service through Mulesoft. Potentially, that ends up reducing the number of transferred prescriptions, renewed prescriptions, and any other paper form prescription that then gets digitized. We're able to remove the manual part of that for all of those or for 85% of them. Then it would probably be somewhere in the realm of $2000 a month.
So we're looking at being able to push 20 plus thousand a year towards something like this. If we were able to get that kind of return out of it or see that kind of potential return.

content.speaker: Speaker 1
content.text: To be crystal clear, the electronic FAS is... So ESOFT is used to extract the data coming through and then it directly into your systems. It wouldn't be the actual effects solution that... Right. We'd be able to monitor the inbox of the ES women.

content.speaker: Speaker 2
content.text:
So... There are a couple of different things from a pharmacy perspective that I've been looking at this from the perspective of we get and we don't have this piece yet, but we get the EFX system set up.
Then Mulesoft is able to capture all of that, transfer that, or transpose all of that information to where it's supposed to go within a new prescription. Then we're just filling the prescriptions, right?
That's the goal. From that perspective, if it has any more broad potential applications than that, then I'd be interested in seeing that because one thing that we do receive is electronic prescriptions all the time.
With those electronic prescriptions, we still oftentimes have to... I can't tell you exactly why or why not. It might have to do with medication history. I just don't know the piece in between.
But sometimes some of that information will transpose automatically and electronically into its correct position, other times it doesn't. Either way, or the vast majority of them, new electronic prescriptions show up. We're manually data entering. At least the electronic prescription instructions.
Then potentially that plus the doctor's name.
